item.title: [IGNITE-2195] Accessing from IGFS to HDFS that is in kerberised environment
item.description:
There is some issue in the current IGFS implementation that doesn't take into account some Kerberos user related settings which leads to the exception below when there is an attempt to work with Kerberised cluster

The issue is fixed in the following way. Need to revisit the fix and check whether it can lead to some other consequences.

/**
* @return {@link org.apache.hadoop.fs.FileSystem}  instance for this secondary Fs.
* @throws IOException
*/
public FileSystem createFileSystem(String userName) throws IOException {
    userName = IgfsUtils.fixUserName(userName);

    UserGroupInformation.setConfiguration(cfg);
    UserGroupInformation ugi = UserGroupInformation.createProxyUser(userName, UserGroupInformation.getCurrentUser());

    try {
        return ugi.doAs(new PrivilegedExceptionAction<FileSystem>() {
            @Override
            public FileSystem run() throws Exception {
                    return FileSystem.get(uri, cfg);
            }
        });
    } catch (InterruptedException e) {
        Thread.currentThread().interrupt();

        throw new IOException("Failed to create file system due to interrupt.", e);
    }
}
item.summary: Accessing from IGFS to HDFS that is in kerberised environment

status.description: The issue is considered finished, the resolution is correct. Issues which are not closed can be reopened.

comments.comment: Quick fix idea is to make org.apache.ignite.internal.processors.hadoop.SecondaryFileSystemProvider pluggable: this way user can substitute it with anything he needs just via Spring configuration.
Attached an implementation of HadoopFileSystemFactory for a kerberised environment. The implementation was already tested in production. Lets contribute it to Apache Ignite.

Pull Request: https://github.com/apache/ignite/pull/464

I suggest a fix without dedicated re-login thread. Each file system operation checks if re-login is necessary and, if so, performs re-login.

Configuration example:

                <bean class="org.apache.ignite.configuration.FileSystemConfiguration" parent="igfsCfgBase">

                 .....
                    <property name="secondaryFileSystem">
                        <bean class="org.apache.ignite.hadoop.fs.IgniteHadoopIgfsSecondaryFileSystem" >
                            <property name="fileSystemFactory">
                                <bean class="org.apache.ignite.hadoop.fs.SecureHadoopFileSystemFactory">
                                     <property name="configPaths" value="/etc/hadoop/conf/core-site.xml"/>
                                     <property name="keyTab" value="/etc/krb5.keytab" />
                                     <property name="keyTabPrincipal" value="foo" />
                                     <property name="reloginInterval" value="#{30 * 60 * 1000}" />
                                </bean>
                            </property>
                        </bean>
                    </property>

My comments:
1) Why is it copypasted from basic factory? Looks like inheritance should be used here instead.
2) reloginIfNeeded() should not be public
3) Is it common practice to use UserGroupInformation.getLoginUser() as real kerberos user?
4) getLoginUser -> loginUserFromSubject -> spawnAutoRenewalThreadForUserCreds() -> new Thread(). Do we aware of it? Can it cause a leak?
5) What does check "!F.isEmpty(keyTab) && !F.isEmpty(keyTabPrincipal)" mean? Looks invalid to me, as UserGroupInformation.loginUserFromKeytab() has both parameters nullable.
6) Why do we synchornize on UserGroupInformation.class? Is it a normal practice?
7) String "UserGroupInformation loginUser = UserGroupInformation.getLoginUser();" should be called only if debug is enabled. Also, this method has side effects, so I doubt it is valid to call it only for debug.
8) Configuration values are not validated anyhow.
9) There are no tests.

1) inherited from Basic factory
2) made protected.
3) to get the user each time with UserGroupInformation.getLoginUser() just seems to be more reliable: this way can be sure that we're in sync with the static context of UserGroupInformation.
4) this thread will be spawned only if the login is performed from the kerberos ticket, but not from the keytab (org.apache.hadoop.security.UserGroupInformation#isKeytab == false), but in SecureHadoopFileSystemFactory we always have isKeytab == true.
5) Now the key tab parameters are validated in start() method, nulls are not allowed.
6) This sync just joins together 2 static synchronized methods, to avoid concurrent invocations between them. This seems to make the code more reliable.
7) removed this code.
8) fixed.
9) Added very simple test that checks only the parameters validation and serialization.

Ivan, my comments:
1) SecureHadoopFileSystemFactorySelfTest.checkSerialization - keytab is not checked.

2) "SecureHadoopFileSystemFactorySelfTest extends TestCase" - unit tests should derive from GridCommonAbstractTest as per our conventions.

3) As we target specific kerberos use case, lets name factory "KerberosHadoopFileSystemFactory", so that it's use case is more clear.

4) "implements HadoopFileSystemFactory, Externalizable, LifecycleAware" should be removed as BasicHadoopFileSystemFactory already implements all these interfaces.

5) SecureHadoopFileSystemFactory docs: "The factory spawns a dedicated thread ..." - this is not the case.

6) Docs for "keyTabPrincipal" - remove "hdfs-Sandbox" as this is a misleading hint for users.

7) DFLT_RELOGIN_INTERVAL should be public - we did that for all other defaults.

8) reloginIfNeeded(): lastReloginTime is updated only if (reloginInterval != 0). Is it normal? As potential implementor of derived class I would be surprised that this field (which is protected) is not updated.

9) Looks like we can get rid of all code duplication in create0() and getFileSystem() methods. The only thing you need is a method to obtain the file system.

BasicHadoopFileSystemFactory:

return FileSystem.get(uri, cfg, usrName);

KerberosHadoopFileSystemFactory:

UserGroupInformation proxyUgi = UserGroupInformation.createProxyUser(userName, UserGroupInformation.getLoginUser());

return proxyUgi.doAs(new PrivilegedExceptionAction<FileSystem>() {
    @Override public FileSystem run() throws Exception {
        return getFileSystem(fullUri, cfg);
    }
});

10) Detailed docs about keytab, keytabPrincipal and relogin interval must be places to corresponding getters, not to fields. Setters, in turn must refer to getters. See BasicHadoopFileSystemFactory.setUri() as example.

11) reloginInterval is not validated. What if user pass negative value? Test is needed for this as well.

12) I would remove synchronization on UserGroupInformation.class because it doesn't add any valuable protection. Anyone is able to overwrite configuration later causing subsequent call to checkTGTAndReloginFromKeytab() to fail. We have no control of it.
